analysis.investment_thesis: Devyani is loss-making (net profit –INR 7 Cr in FY25 despite INR 4,951 Cr revenue), carries D/E of 1.71x, and generates ROCE of only 6.42% — all three of which are automatic disqualifiers under the Magic Formula. A Forward P/E of 127x for a restaurant operator with a history of recurring losses is simply not a price I will pay.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 19.3% over 9 years demonstrates strong unit economics growth in the Indian QSR market under KFC and Pizza Hut franchises
OCF has been consistently positive (5/5 years, INR 900 Cr in FY25), showing the restaurant-level cash generation is real even if bottom-line profits are elusive
Promoter holding of 61.37% provides alignment, and DII ownership of 19.44% reflects domestic institutional confidence
key_risks: Net profit has been negative in 7 of the last 10 years — the Magic Formula cannot operate on companies without sustained positive EBIT reaching the bottom line; finance costs of INR 267 Cr erode all operating profit

Debt/Equity of 1.71x is dangerously high for a restaurant operator; total borrowings hit INR 3,343 Cr in FY25, nearly double the FY24 figure — rapid debt accumulation for store expansion is concerning
ROCE of 6.42% means the company is earning well below its cost of capital — every rupee invested generates only 6 paise of operating return, making economic value destruction the base case
red_flags: Negative net profit in FY24 (–INR 10 Cr) and FY25 (–INR 7 Cr) despite revenue growing to INR 4,951 Cr — operating leverage is not materializing as expansion costs accelerate
Finance costs of INR 267 Cr in FY25 (vs. INR 149 Cr in FY23) are growing faster than revenues — the debt-funded expansion model is self-defeating if ROIC stays below the cost of debt
EV/EBITDA of 28x for a company with negative net income implies pure hope valuation; any normalization of growth expectations would be devastating to the share price
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula calculation: EV = INR 13,279 + 3,188 – 181 = INR 16,286 Cr. Operating Income FY25 = INR 839 Cr (but note: under Ind AS 116, restaurant lease costs are capitalized, making EBITDA look better than true cash economics). Earnings Yield = 5.15% at the operating level, but net profit is negative — the true earnings yield is essentially zero. ROCE = 6.42%. Both metrics fail the Magic Formula test comprehensively.

QSR businesses can be wonderful — high turnover, relatively asset-light, strong brands. But Devyani is a franchise operator, not a franchise owner, and it's funding aggressive store expansion with debt while posting recurring losses. The P&L tells me the unit economics aren't strong enough to overcome overhead and interest burden at scale. Until the company demonstrates 3+ years of sustained positive net income and ROCE above 15%, this doesn't belong in my portfolio at any price, let alone at Forward P/E of 127x.
